name: Sprengel Deformity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Sprengel Deformity

criteria.description: Congenital elevation of the scapula compared to the contralateral side
Hypoplasia or dysplasia of the scapula on imaging studies
Limited abduction and elevation of the shoulder joint
Presence of an omovertebral bone connecting scapula to cervical spine on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital scapular elevation with radiological evidence of scapular hypoplasia; omovertebral bone is supportive but not required
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; associated anomalies should be evaluated.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of the shoulder girdle musculature

imaging: Elevated scapula on chest X-ray or shoulder radiographs
Hypoplastic scapula with abnormal shape on CT or MRI
Omovertebral bone connecting scapula to cervical spine on imaging
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromes such as Klippel-Feil
other: Physical examination revealing asymmetric shoulder height and limited shoulder range of motion

distinguishingFeatures: Short neck with limited neck movement
May have Sprengel deformity as associated feature

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating cervical spinal cord compression
Respiratory distress due to thoracic deformity
Severe limitation of shoulder function impacting daily activities
references: Sprengel Deformity: Clinical Features and Management. Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics, 2020.
Radiological assessment of Sprengel deformity. Skeletal Radiology, 2018.
